task: Edit this fictional club-news data paragraph in about 80–120 words. Use the supplied definitions to distinguish membership status at a date from renewals during a quarter. Correct the percentage's label without inventing a renewal-rate denominator or an attendance count.
input: The club achieved a 75 percent renewal rate this quarter: 180 of its 240 registered members renewed. Another 140 people attended sessions. These figures prove that most members came back because of the new programme.

facts.text: The synthetic register lists 240 members as of 31 March 2026.
Of those members, 180 are classified as active.
Active means having booked at least one session during the preceding year.
The active share of the register is 75 percent.
The club processed 140 membership renewals during January–March 2026.
The packet does not supply the number of memberships eligible for renewal during that quarter.
The packet supplies no attendance total or reason for renewal.

forbidden_additions: The active-member percentage relabelled as a renewal rate.
Renewals relabelled as attendees or visits.
An invented eligible-renewal denominator, causal explanation, or programme-success finding.
preserve: The date-specific register and the separate quarterly renewal count.
The supplied operational definition of active.
The correct 180-of-240 calculation without assigning it to the wrong measure.
